content_selection.rationale: Most of the included stories hold up. The Replit/Anthropic dispute got wide pickup. Beam's actual Apache-2.0 weight release did happen on Oct 16, after its Oct 5 announcement, so including it is justified. The FTC demands and Muse Spark Open were reasonably left out because they appeared to be already covered in the prior brief. The weak spots are two headline-only arXiv items (Sci-Pivot, RealtimeBench), which carry little news value. Meanwhile, important Oct 15–16 policy news never appears even on the candidate list: China's draft export controls on 23 AI technologies, and the White House Super Intelligence task force adopting its charter and starting a 120-day risk-report clock. A better-covered DeepMind agent result (Gemini 4 Argon beating Minecraft) was also cut in favor of obscure papers.
content_selection.evidence: The brief includes '🔬 Sci-Pivot benchmark... (headline-only)' and 'RealtimeBench... (headline-only)'. Meanwhile, MOFCOM on Oct 16 'published a draft that adds 23 artificial intelligence technologies, including large models, agents and computing clusters' to its export-restriction catalogue. That story is missing from the candidate list.

selection_disagreements.story: China MOFCOM/MOST draft export controls on 23 AI technologies (Oct 16)
selection_disagreements.rationale: My search found that on Oct 16 Beijing published a draft adding large models, agents and computing clusters to its prohibited/restricted export catalogue. It also requires temporary export registration right away, with comments open until Nov 15. This is a major geopolitical AI policy move. The research process never surfaced it, and it clearly outranks the headline-only arXiv items.

selection_disagreements.story: White House Super Intelligence task force adopts charter, starts 120-day AI risk report (Oct 15–16)
selection_disagreements.rationale: Semafor, via AI Weekly, and FDD's overnight brief report that the task force formally adopted its charter. Its first meeting started a 120-day window for a risk report on cybersecurity, biosecurity and model control. This fits directly with the brief's own agent-containment and FTC thread, but it never appeared as a candidate.
It is a headline-only arXiv benchmark with no detail fetched, and I found no wider coverage. It takes a slot that more consequential policy news should have filled.
This is also a headline-only arXiv paper with a narrow result. Its value is low next to the missed policy stories and the excluded, more widely covered Gemini 4 Argon Minecraft result.

selection_disagreements.story: Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft (DeepMind, arXiv 2610.22319)
selection_disagreements.rationale: AI Weekly's Oct 16 edition featured it prominently: four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat the Ender Dragon from a random spawn in about 27 hours, writing 2,783 programs. It is a more notable lab result than the two headline-only benchmarks that made the brief.

factual_accuracy.rationale: I checked every section against its primary source: Axios (both articles), the Artificial Analysis Beam and Vera Rubin articles, the TechCrunch articles on Replit, Elorian and CERT-In, The Register's Postgres story, Vercel's October index, and the arXiv abstracts for Athanor, SciΠvot and RealtimeBench. Every number, date, quote and model name I checked matched. The brief kept the important caveats, including the insider dispute over Replit, Glimpse results coming from Elorian's own evaluations, Gartner figures being forecasts, the gateway under-counting direct API traffic, and the agents' results being unreplicated. The only discrepancies are trivial: the arXiv papers were submitted October 15 and appeared in the October 16 listings, and the brief does not mention that Gartner's own headline number (over $3.5T exposed to impairment by 2030) differs from the Axios framing it reports ($4T by 2032).
factual_accuracy.evidence: Brief: 'Global AI-related debt issuance fell to $23 billion in September from $113 billion in June, per the Financial Times as cited by Axios' — Axios: 'Global AI-related debt issuance plunged to $23 billion in September 2026, down sharply from $113 billion in June, per the Financial Times.'

length_format.rationale: The brief has 11 Headlines bullets, inside the 8-15 range, and 9 deep-dives (Research 3, Industry 2, Products 2, Benchmarks 1, Policy 1), inside the 5-10 range. All required sections are present and none is padded. The main deviation is per-item length: most deep-dives run 7-8 sentences, past the stated 3-6 maximum, because they append 'Why it matters' and caveat sentences. A few headline bullets also carry long follow-up cross-references that make them less skimmable. Counts and structure comply, but the repeated per-item overrun is a moderate format breach.
length_format.evidence: The debt-boom deep-dive has about 8 sentences (Axios reports… / It cites Gartner… / Global AI-related debt issuance… / About $18 billion… / Axios says… / The counterpoints… / Why it matters… / The Gartner figures are forecasts.). The Beam, Athanor, Replit, PostgreSQL and Vera Rubin items each run about 7.
